2027-05-19.title: First Wednesday of the Apostles
2027-05-19.readTitle: Readings of the day (First Set; mapped from the official calendar, verify locally)
readings: When you come together to eat, wait for one another
The mustard seed and the yeast
2027-05-19.alt: Season of the Apostles (Šleehe), the seven weeks that begin at Pentecost. The Holy Qurbana is celebrated with the Anaphora of Addai and Mari; from Pentecost “The Angel of the Lord” (the Angelus) is prayed again in place of the Queen of Heaven. The calendar gives the Epistle as 1 Corinthians 11:31–34a. The Syro-Malankara calendar today recalls the tradition of the first offering of the Holy Qurbono by Mar Yaqob Shleeha.
2027-05-19.verse: The kingdom of heaven is like a mustard seed that someone took and sowed in his field;
theo: Three days after Pentecost, in the first week of the Season of the Apostles, the Gospel gives us two small parables about the growth of the Church. “The kingdom of heaven is like a mustard seed that someone took and sowed in his field; it is the smallest of all the seeds, but when it has grown it is the greatest of shrubs and becomes a tree, so that the birds of the air come and make nests in its branches.” Think of the beginning: about one hundred and twenty people in an upper room, a handful of fishermen, a few women, the Mother of Jesus. Think of what came of it: on the day of Pentecost three thousand, and within a few generations communities from Spain to Persia and, as our tradition holds, to the coast of Malabar. The image of the tree in whose branches the birds nest comes from the prophets. Ezekiel saw God plant a tender sprig on the mountain of Israel, so that it would become a noble cedar: “Under it every kind of bird will live” (Ezekiel 17:23). The birds are the nations. Our Church, which began, as tradition holds, with the preaching of Mar Thoma among a few families of Malabar, is one of those branches. That is not a reason for pride but for gratitude, and for patience: God's work begins small and grows slowly, and it is God who gives the growth.

The second parable is even more hidden. “The kingdom of heaven is like yeast that a woman took and mixed in with three measures of flour until all of it was leavened.” Three measures of flour is a great quantity, enough bread for a large household; it is what Sarah prepared when the three visitors came to Abraham (Genesis 18:6). The yeast disappears into the dough; no one sees it working, yet nothing stays as it was. So the Gospel works in the world: not usually through spectacle, but through Christians mixed into ordinary life, in offices and fields, in hospitals and classrooms, in families, quietly changing everything from within. Matthew adds that Jesus spoke in parables to fulfil the prophecy: “I will open my mouth to speak in parables; I will proclaim what has been hidden from the foundation of the world.” What was hidden from the beginning is God's plan to gather all peoples into one, and Pentecost has revealed it. The apostles were the first yeast; today it is our turn to be mixed into the dough of our society without losing our flavour.

Paul's words to the Corinthians concern the Lord's Supper, and they come right after his account of its institution. Some in Corinth were eating their own meal before the poor arrived, so that “one goes hungry and another becomes drunk.” Paul warns: “But if we judged ourselves, we would not be judged.” And he gives a simple rule: “So then, my brothers and sisters, when you come together to eat, wait for one another.” Before we receive the Body of the Lord, we examine ourselves; our Church has always taught that one who is conscious of grave sin should first approach the sacrament of Reconciliation. And the Body we receive makes us one body with the poor, the late, the one who has nothing to bring. The mustard seed and the yeast grow in a community that waits for one another. It is fitting that the Syro-Malankara calendar recalls today the tradition of the first offering of the Holy Qurbono by Mar Yaqob Shleeha in Jerusalem: from that small first breaking of bread, the Eucharist of the apostles has spread like yeast through the whole world, and it reaches our altar every day.
outline: One hundred and twenty in an upper room, and the Church across the world.
Small beginnings, the great tree and the birds of every nation.
Point 2 · The yeast in three measures of flour
Hidden, mixed in, changing everything from within.
Examining ourselves, and the Eucharist that makes us one with the poor.
“The kingdom of heaven is like a mustard seed.”
live: Begin one small good thing today, a daily prayer, a visit, a saving for the poor, and trust God with its growth.
At the next family meal or parish gathering, make sure the last and least are served first.
fathers: Christ himself is the grain of mustard seed: small and despised in his Passion, but when crushed he poured out his power, and buried in the earth he rose as a tree whose branches shelter all who believe.

The leaven, though small, changes the whole lump when it is mixed in; so the apostles, twelve men, leavened the whole world. But the leaven must be mixed in, not kept apart: we must go among others and not lose our strength.
magis: Jesus' invitation to enter his kingdom comes in the form of parables; through them he invites people to the feast of the kingdom and asks for a radical choice.

To respond to the invitation to Communion we must prepare ourselves; St Paul urges an examination of conscience, and anyone conscious of grave sin must receive the sacrament of Reconciliation before coming to Communion.
The Eucharist commits us to the poor; to receive in truth the Body and Blood of Christ given up for us, we must recognise Christ in the poorest, his brethren.
2027-05-19.prayer: Lord Jesus Christ, you compared the kingdom to a mustard seed and to a little yeast. Make your Church grow from small beginnings into a tree that shelters every nation, and make us yeast hidden in the dough of our society, changing it from within. Teach us to examine ourselves before we come to your table, and to wait for one another, especially for the poor and the last. Glory to you, with the Father and the Holy Spirit, for ever. Amen.
altar: In every Holy Qurbana a little bread, a few grains of wheat, becomes the Body of Christ, and that small host feeds the whole Church. The mustard seed and the yeast are present on our altar.

quick: The kingdom is like a mustard seed, the smallest seed, which becomes a tree where birds nest.
It is like yeast mixed into three measures of flour until all is leavened.
Paul: judge yourselves before the Lord's Supper, and when you come together to eat, wait for one another.
2027-05-19.action: Begin one small good thing today and trust God with its growth.
2027-05-19.question: Am I yeast that is mixed into the world around me, or do I keep my faith apart from my daily life?

family.explain: Jesus said that the kingdom of God is like a tiny mustard seed. It is so small you can hardly see it, but it grows into a big plant, and birds come to build nests in it. It is also like a little yeast that a woman puts into flour, and soon the whole dough rises. The Church began with only a few friends of Jesus, and now it is everywhere in the world, even in our village. Small things done with love can grow very big with God.
family.intention: We pray for missionaries who plant the Gospel in new places, and for small Christian communities that feel weak.
family.ask: Ask: “What small good thing can each of us start this week?”

illus: In the 1970s a nursing sister from Kerala was sent to a village in the north of India where there were no Christians. She had a small dispensary, a bicycle and a rosary. For years she treated fevers and delivered babies, and almost no one asked about her faith. When she retired, the village elders came to thank her, and one of them, a Hindu grandfather, said, “Sister, we never became like you in religion, but you have made our whole village more kind.” Some years later a few families asked a priest to teach them about Jesus. The sister heard the news in her convent in Kerala and said only, “The yeast takes its time.”

pm.open: Lord Jesus, you plant the kingdom like a mustard seed and hide it like yeast in the dough. As we gather in your name, make us small and faithful, and let your kingdom grow in us. Amen.
share: It is the smallest of all the seeds, but when it has grown it is the greatest of shrubs (Matthew 13:32). What small beginning is God asking of me?
Yeast that a woman took and mixed in with three measures of flour (Matthew 13:33). Where am I called to be yeast in my workplace or neighbourhood?
If we judged ourselves, we would not be judged (1 Corinthians 11:31). How do I prepare myself before Holy Communion?
When you come together to eat, wait for one another (1 Corinthians 11:33). Who is left behind in our parish or family?
pm.resp: Lord, let your kingdom grow among us.
interc: For the Church in this Season of the Apostles, that she may grow like the mustard seed and shelter all peoples.
For missionaries and for small Christian communities in difficult places.
For Christians in public life and work, that they may be yeast for justice and kindness.
For the poor and those who are left out at our gatherings, that we may wait for them and serve them first.
For all who will receive Holy Communion this week, that they may prepare with humble hearts.
pm.close: Father, your kingdom grows from the smallest seed and works like hidden yeast. Make us faithful in small things, ready to receive your Son worthily, and attentive to one another. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

homily: Dear friends, three days after Pentecost Jesus tells us how his Church grows. “The kingdom of heaven is like a mustard seed” (Matthew 13:31), the smallest of seeds, that becomes a tree where the birds of the air make their nests.

The Church began with about one hundred and twenty people in an upper room. Today she is in every land, and the birds of every nation find shelter in her branches. Our own Church in Kerala began, as tradition holds, with Mar Thoma and a few families. God's work starts small and grows slowly, and it is God who gives the growth.

Then Jesus says the kingdom is like yeast mixed into three measures of flour until all is leavened (13:33). Yeast is hidden, but it changes everything. Christians are meant to be such yeast in offices, fields, schools and homes: not apart from the world, but mixed into it, without losing their strength.

Paul warns the Corinthians about their Lord's Supper: “if we judged ourselves, we would not be judged” (1 Corinthians 11:31). Before we receive the Body of the Lord we examine our conscience. And he adds: “when you come together to eat, wait for one another” (11:33). The Eucharist makes us one body with the poor and the last.
So let us not despise small beginnings, let us be yeast in the world, and let us come to the Holy Qurbana prepared and attentive to one another. Amen.
kids: Children, a mustard seed is tiny, like a speck of dust, but it grows into a big plant where birds can sit! Jesus says small good things done with love grow big with God. What small good thing will you do today?

intro: Theme: “The kingdom of heaven is like a mustard seed that someone took and sowed in his field;”
The Church growing from small beginnings, the hidden yeast that changes the world, and a Eucharistic community that waits for one another.

points.h: The smallest of all the seeds
sub: One hundred and twenty in an upper room.
The tree where the birds nest.
q: On the mountain height of Israel I will plant it, in order that it may produce boughs and bear fruit, and become a noble cedar. Under it every kind of bird will live;
it is the smallest of all the seeds, but when it has grown it is the greatest of shrubs and becomes a tree, so that the birds of the air come and make nests in its branches.
points.apply: Begin one small, faithful practice this week and keep it every day.

q: For whoever has despised the day of small things shall rejoice,
The kingdom of heaven is like yeast that a woman took and mixed in with three measures of flour until all of it was leavened.
points.apply: Do one hidden act of goodness each day this week at your work or school, without telling anyone.

q: Search me, O God, and know my heart; test me and know my thoughts.
So then, my brothers and sisters, when you come together to eat, wait for one another.
points.apply: Make a careful examination of conscience before your next Holy Communion, and go to confession if you need to.

concl: The Church of the apostles grows like a seed and works like yeast, and her heart is a table where all wait for one another.
Let us be faithful in small things, hidden and active in the world, and prepared at the altar.
2027-05-19.resolve: This week, keep one small daily practice, do one hidden good deed each day, and prepare well for Holy Communion.
